memory_update.text: HealthStream should be promoted to the underfollowed discovery lane for healthcare workforce education capacity because it links nursing schools, clinical placement workflows, credentialing, clinical education, and healthcare employer workforce systems.
CAE is a possible second-order simulation-capacity supplier, but the healthcare segment may be too small relative to total company; later layers must test materiality.

Healthcare education capacity is constrained by more than student demand: clinical placements, simulation infrastructure, program approvals, licensure alignment, and nursing-school workflow software may be separate chokepoints.

Private vendors appear important in clinical placement, licensure prep, and healthcare education content; public-market mapping may be sparse, making HSTM and CAE more relevant despite imperfect purity.

node: Healthcare workforce education capacity: nursing, behavioral health, counseling, social work, occupational therapy, and licensure programs
summary: Layer 1B expands the healthcare-workforce education capacity node using a two-lane funnel. Reference names are GCE and CVSA because they directly operate or support scaled healthcare/licensure education. The underfollowed lane highlights second-order suppliers that may benefit from nursing and clinical-program capacity expansion without taking direct Title IV enrollment risk: HealthStream for clinical placement, learning, credentialing, and nursing-school workflow software; and CAE for healthcare simulation hardware/software that can substitute for scarce clinical training capacity. Claims are labeled conservatively; later layers should verify segment revenue exposure, customer concentration, program-level adoption, and whether healthcare education growth is material enough to move company-level fundamentals.
